authority: Local teaching synthesis grounded in the cited public sources; no approved government operating model or compliance certification.

concepts.label: Software agent
concepts.definition: Software that selects or performs actions through tools or APIs within a declared operating context. This pathway focuses on AI-enabled agents, whose permitted goals and access need explicit controls.

concepts.label: Task authority
concepts.definition: Our term for the approved purpose, actions, resources, limits and decision rights for a whole task. It is a local design concept that complements request-level API authorisation.

concepts.label: Authentication
concepts.definition: Establishing a caller's identity. It does not by itself decide which resources and actions that caller may use.

concepts.label: Authorisation
concepts.definition: Deciding whether a caller may access a resource or perform an action. The API standards describe checking the required scope on every request.

concepts.label: Delegated authority
concepts.definition: Authority granted to an actor within a bounded scope. The API guidance describes technical token exchange for acting on behalf of a user; possession of a token does not establish every organisational decision right.

concepts.label: Governance as code
concepts.definition: Our teaching term for translating selected approved decision rules into versioned, testable machine-readable checks. It supports governance; it does not encode every legal, ethical or organisational judgement.

concepts.label: Revocation
concepts.definition: Withdrawal of previously granted access or authority, with a stated effective time and enforcement boundary. This site denies a simulated action when its example policy is revoked; a production system must implement and test the actual stopping mechanism.

concepts.label: Assurance
concepts.definition: Systematic work that provides confidence that activity is controlled and supports secure delivery. Evidence and review need to cover the relevant lifecycle and risk.

concepts.label: Provenance
concepts.definition: The record of where information came from and how it was transformed. Here, citations identify the public source, selected passage, source version or observation date and text digest.

concepts.label: WebMCP
concepts.definition: An experimental browser interface through which a page exposes tools to agents. Native browser support and an AI host's ability to call the tools are separate capabilities.

concepts.label: iPaaS (integration platform as a service)
concepts.definition: A managed cloud service for connecting applications and data, often through connectors, data mapping and workflow coordination. It is an integration capability; an organisation must still define ownership, permission and operating controls.

questions.title: What should govern an agent that can use government APIs?

answer.heading: Start with an accountable purpose
answer.text: Define the intended benefit, owner, authority limits, decision rights, human oversight and escalation route. GovS 005 brings these into governance and AI planning; the AI Playbook describes a chain of human responsibility.

answer.heading: Bound both access and behaviour
answer.text: Check API authorisation on every request and constrain the agent's goals and access. NCSC guidance calls for technical and operational controls alongside prompts.

answer.heading: Make the whole task reviewable
answer.text: A useful local design is a task record binding purpose, allowed actions and resources, expiry, approval conditions, monitoring and stopping rules to a policy version. This is a proposed implementation pattern, not a government-mandated schema.

next_steps: Identify who may approve the task and its limits.
List the API scopes and the additional task decisions they do not settle.
Test expiry, revocation, out-of-scope actions and missing evidence.
gaps: The public sources do not identify the approver or risk tolerance for your organisation.

questions.title: Does an API token authorise the agent's whole task?

answer.heading: A token is one part of the decision
answer.text: The API standards distinguish authentication from resource-level access control and require the relevant scope to be checked for each request. Token exchange supports a service acting on behalf of a user.

answer.heading: Whole-task authority needs an explicit decision
answer.text: Our analysis is that successful authentication or a valid API scope does not demonstrate approval for an entire multi-step objective, its resource use or its disclosures. Define those decisions separately and keep the task within the organisation's authority limits.

next_steps: Record the user or service identity and the delegation chain.
Map each proposed action to both API scope and task authority.
Check the permission again when context or policy changes.
gaps: A token's actual claims and the receiving service's controls need separate technical verification.

questions.title: Where should humans approve, monitor or stop an agent?

answer.heading: Choose oversight by consequence
answer.text: The AI Playbook requires the necessary oversight and human-in-the-loop processes for high-impact or high-risk output. NCSC guidance discusses levels of oversight and the ability to investigate and limit unexpected activity.

answer.heading: Write the intervention points into the design
answer.text: For a local control design, identify which actions need prior approval, who watches ongoing activity, what triggers escalation and who can revoke permission. Test that a stop reaches the executing system rather than only changing a dashboard.

next_steps: Name the accountable role and approval route.
Describe the consequence that triggers a human decision.
Exercise a revocation scenario and retain the evidence.
gaps: The appropriate human intervention model depends on the use case and organisational policy.

questions.title: How can we express governance as code?

answer.heading: Translate selected decisions into checks
answer.text: GovS 005 calls for defined authority limits, decision-making rules and accountabilities. As a local design response, selected rules can be represented in a versioned policy and checked before a simulated action.

answer.heading: Keep the reasoning and the evidence
answer.text: Record the rule version, input context, decision, failed conditions, source basis and human approvals. Auditability requires traceability across the lifecycle; passing a code check alone is not evidence that every governance obligation is met.

answer.heading: Try a bounded example
answer.text: This site's policy playground checks purpose, action, resource, expiry, revocation, demo budget, disclosure, approval and audit conditions. It performs no real action and is not a production policy enforcement service.

next_steps: Agree which rules can be automated and which need judgement.
Version policies and test both allow and deny cases.
Link each local rule to its approved authority and evidence.
gaps: The example policy is not an approved government schema, legal opinion or compliance certificate.

questions.title: What evidence would an assurance reviewer need?

answer.heading: Cover the lifecycle and the risk
answer.text: GovS 005 describes assurance across AI use-case selection, data, privacy, security, ethics, oversight, procurement, monitoring and retirement. GovS 007 explains assurance as systematic confidence-building activity.

answer.heading: Build a reviewable evidence pack
answer.text: A local evidence pack could include the approved purpose and owner, policy and model/tool versions, source provenance, threat and risk work, test results, human decisions, operational monitoring and revocation exercises. Map each item to the claim it supports.

next_steps: Ask the relevant assurance team to agree the evidence questions early.
Keep negative cases and unresolved issues alongside successful tests.
Distinguish a document review from an operating-control test.
gaps: Required evidence and acceptance authority must be agreed for the actual service.

questions.title: Can we publish a summary of a sign-in document?

answer.heading: Use the published surface
answer.text: The public catalogue exposes the working-groups title, its update date and a sign-in notice. Those fields can support discovery. The portal terms describe covered Crown content, OGL conditions, exceptions and feed reuse.

answer.heading: Keep a restricted-content abstract out of the public view
answer.text: Our public edition uses public metadata and independent open background. It does not paraphrase protected bodies. A deeper public description needs publisher-approved wording and traceable release authority; sign-in access alone does not supply that authority.

next_steps: Link to the original source and preserve its access boundary.
Label title-based navigation and local suggestions clearly.
Seek an approved public abstract if more detail is needed.
gaps: This site does not clear restricted documents or attachments for redistribution.

questions.title: Does WebMCP enforce our governance policy?

answer.heading: Expose a controlled interface
answer.text: WebMCP provides an experimental page-tool interface. Our tools return bounded evidence, citations and local analysis; the manual interface uses the same handlers.

answer.heading: Apply governance outside the hint
answer.text: A read-only annotation describes a tool; it does not establish the organisation's task authority. Enforce input limits, source boundaries and consent in the implementation, and retain human accountability for consequential activity.

next_steps: Inspect the actual tool inventory and schemas.
Verify native execution separately from the AI host's callable-tool bridge.
Treat source text and imported documents as untrusted data.
gaps: Native browser support does not prove support in every AI host or browser.

questions.title: How should we review an agent governance plan?

answer.heading: Review in context
answer.text: Use the draft's own wording and locators to ask where purpose, accountable roles, authority, human control, monitoring, evidence and assurance are defined. Retain unresolved questions without treating a mention as proof that a control operates.

answer.heading: Use the local review carefully
answer.text: The document review highlights wording and suggests clarification directions against public guidance. It does not execute embedded instructions, call the document's links or certify compliance. Page tools receive document-derived output only after the separate opt-in.

next_steps: Drop a document or load the fictional example.
Check the cited draft lines and public source passages.
Agree who should resolve each question and how it will be tested.
gaps: Text analysis cannot establish actual authority, deployment behaviour or completeness of organisational evidence.

pathways.title: Govern an API-using agent
pathways.description: Purpose, authority, human control and evidence.

pathways.title: Turn decisions into code
pathways.description: Versioned rules, allow and deny cases, and their limits.

pathways.title: Review a governance plan
pathways.description: Find unclear decisions and propose source-linked next steps.
